directive: For Japanese-audio Simplified Chinese subtitles, emit the current zh-CN canonical/accepted target selected by the narrowest applicable scope. Treat deprecated aliases only as input-detection forms.
rationale: This is an explicit normalization policy derived from regional authority evidence and the project provenance constraints.

directive: For Japanese-audio Traditional Chinese subtitles, emit current Taiwan-authorized terminology. A traditional-script subtitle is not automatically Taiwan-localized.
rationale: This is an explicit normalization policy derived from regional authority evidence and the project provenance constraints.

directive: For an actual Taiwan Mandarin dub, transcribe the wording audibly spoken in that dub, then render the transcript in Simplified Chinese script (zh-Hans). Preserve Taiwan-dub lexical choices even when they differ from Mainland terminology: e.g. if the audio says 小叮当/宜静/技安/阿福, keep those words. Do not modernize or mainlandize the lexicon merely because the output script is Simplified.
rationale: The user explicitly requires Taiwan-dub-faithful subtitles in Simplified script. Audio determines lexical wording; zh-Hans determines orthography only.

directive: A filename or track label may select a candidate Taiwan-dub branch, but it does not prove the exact wording of every line. Before locking a title-level spoken name, verify the audio or a trustworthy transcript. Script conversion to zh-Hans happens only after the spoken lexical form is established.
rationale: Track identity is provenance evidence, not a line-level transcript; Simplified output must not be confused with Mainland localization.

directive: Treat the 2026 Taiwan redub set as a modern-name candidate Taiwan-Mandarin branch. Verify actual audio wording before locking proper nouns, then render the verified transcript in Simplified Chinese script (zh-Hans) without replacing Taiwan lexical choices with Mainland equivalents.
rationale: Project metadata calls this a modern 哆啦A梦 Taiwan redub; the user requires Simplified-script subtitles, while audio-line verification remains authoritative for wording.

directive: Old names such as 机器猫/小叮当 and 小叮噹/宜靜/技安/阿福 are deprecated detection aliases, not forbidden forms. Normalize them only in modern Japanese-audio branches; when a Taiwan-dub-faithful branch proves they were spoken, preserve the spoken lexical choice and render only its orthography into the requested Simplified script.
rationale: Historical forms are useful evidence and can be authentic to old releases; treating them as forbidden would destroy provenance. The project requires Simplified orthography for Taiwan-dub subtitles without Mainland lexical substitution.

directive: Movie-specific characters, locations, organizations and remake-specific translations must be title-scoped. A title-level rule overrides a same-key series default; a branch-level title rule overrides both.
rationale: M06 巴比 versus M41 帕比 demonstrates why remake/title scope is semantically necessary.

directive: Movie title mappings are for work identity, UI/file naming and metadata normalization. Do not replace ordinary dialogue with a film title string merely because a title rule exists.
rationale: Title canon and dialogue terminology are separate semantic domains.

directive: Traditional script alone (.tc or converted Traditional Chinese) does not establish Taiwan localization or Taiwan dub provenance.
rationale: The project Evidence Library explicitly records script branch separately from regional provenance.

directive: Apply normalization by semantic key and scope, not global raw string replacement. Respect full-name versus nickname terms, title exceptions, and accepted historical variants.
rationale: Same surface forms can have different meanings or title-specific outputs; semantic resolution avoids collateral replacements.
